    dy1 = yp1 - yp0
    dx2 = xp3 - xp2
    dy2 = yp3 - yp2
    
    # Solve for t and u in:
    # p0 + t * (p1-p0) = p2 + u * (p3-p2)
    denom = dx1 * dy2 - dy1 * dx2

        # Parallel or collinear

        cross1 = (xp2 - xp0) * dy1 - (yp2 - yp0) * dx1

        def dot(ax, ay, bx, by):

        # Project onto s1 direction

        tmin, tmax = min(t2, t3), max(t2, t3)

    yp1 = float(data[idx]); idx+=1

    dx1 = xp1 - xp0
    dy1 = yp1 - yp0
    dx2 = xp3 - xp2
    dy2 = yp3 - yp2
    
    # D = dx1*(-dy2) + dx2*dy1
    D = -dx1*dy2 + dx2*dy1
    
    if abs(D) < 1e-10:
        # Parallel or collinear - handle edge case
        # If collinear, any point on overlap works
        # For now, just print one endpoint

        return

import sys

def main():
    data = list(map(float, sys.stdin.read().strip().split()))
    if len(data) != 8:
        return

    x0, y0, x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3 = data

    # Line s1: p0 + t * (p1 - p0)
    # Line s2: p2 + u * (p3 - p2)
    dx1 = x1 - x0
    dy1 = y1 - y0
    dx2 = x3 - x2
    dy2 = y3 - y2

    # Cross product denominator
    den = dx1 * dy2 - dy1 * dx2

    # Since the problem guarantees an intersection point, den != 0
    t = ((x2 - x0) * dy2 - (y2 - y0) * dx2) / den

    ix = x0 + t * dx1
    iy = y0 + t * dy1

    print(f"{ix:.10f} {iy:.10f}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
